mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in CPIAUCSL above 3% over two consecutive quarters signals persistent inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates, which reduces present value of future corporate cash flows and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL exceeds 3% for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in UNRATE below 4% for three consecutive months signals weakening labor demand, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of triggered episodes during labor market softening.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 of more than 2% signals a contraction in aggregate demand, which depresses corporate revenues and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 40% of GDP contraction episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in INDPRO above its 12-month moving average by more than 1.5% signals improving industrial production, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not statistically different from zero in INDPRO-led recovery episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in FEDFUNDS and a decline in RSAFS above 5% from prior quarter indicates tightening monetary policy and reduced liquidity, which depresses risk asset valuations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises and RSAFS falls > 5% QoQ
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of tightening episodes defined by this trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in GDPC1 and HOUST above their 3-month moving averages signals strengthening housing and overall demand, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are not significantly above zero during these co-movements.

mechanism_narrative: When PAYEMS rises while UNRATE falls, it indicates job creation occurring alongside weaker wage growth, which typically precedes margin expansion and higher earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not statistically different from baseline during such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation exists between rising INDPRO and rising S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days in any macro regime, as industrial production growth signals broad economic expansion and higher corporate profits.
failure_condition: The correlation between INDPRO growth and S&P 500 60-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.10) in out-of-sample data.
